correctness.rationale: Gaussian prime Euler factors are S_a(Nπ^{-2}), and ζ_{Q(i)}(2)=ζ(2)L(2,χ-4) includes one norm-2 ramified prime and split norms with multiplicity two. For every nonramified norm below 29 an independently implemented exact Fraction tail product through norm 113 exceeds 1+n^{-2}; the smallest margin is 0.00006504 at the second norm-5 factor. The complete 66-anchor prime chain was independently trial-divided and checked q_next^2<2q_prev^2 from 29 past 8e9. Bennett et al Theorem 1.2, table q=4, bounds theta(x;4,1) by an error <=x/(840 log x) for x>=8e9, giving q in (x,sqrt(2)x) and hence two later split factors with combined 1+2q^-2>1+n^-2. The overlap lemma therefore fills [1,C]. The norm-2 Euler factor values S_a(1/4), a>=1, yield overlapping intervals [5/4,Z] since C>(25/24)^2>21/20; C<5/4 by ζ(2)*β(2)<10/6. Infinite result follows from analytic bound and interval lemma, not extrapolated chain.

value.rationale: An exact determination of all connected components and the unique missing range interval for a natural Gaussian analogue of generalized divisor sums is a motivated arithmetic-topology invariant. Gaussian prime splitting changes the integer-case answer (three components at ordinary σ_-2) to exactly two and requires nontrivial unconditional progression control plus exact finite tail products. This is neither a known integer table recomputation nor an arbitrary numerical slice.
residual_risks: The computation covers only Z[i] and reciprocal fourth power, not other imaginary quadratic UFDs or analytic densities.

final_claim: For the Gaussian divisor sum δ_{-4}(z)=sum over unit classes of divisors |d|^{-4} on nonzero Z[i], the closure of its full real range is exactly [1,(3/4)ζ(2)L(2,χ_{-4})] union [5/4,ζ(2)L(2,χ_{-4})]; the two closed intervals are disjoint and exhaustive.
